influences.name: Vicky Balcou
influences.context: My mother was a graphic illustrator in the sixties and a solo parent, which was incredibly pioneering for her and then eventually became the head designer for Fitz Floyd for the last - for 25 years. And now she is an active, showing fine artist in the Texas area.

influences.name: Luis Jimenez
influences.context: my father is - was an internationally known sculptor named Luis Jimenez

influences.name: Elicia Jimenez
influences.context: my grandmother, Elicia Jimenez, who I knew as mejah, she taught me to sew from the time I was like two all the way up. And she would have to say was one of my early super fan girls and that she always encouraged me to follow my heart and to do what I believed in.

influences.name: Holly Solomon
influences.context: I got represented by Holly Solomon during the last, like, 8 to 10 years of her life and being, you know, being represented by one of the three heavy hitters of the eighties art world was like a dream come true. And she was an incredible mentor.

influences.name: John Coltrane
influences.context: I re-immersed myself in the music of John and Alice Coltrane. I was suddenly struck by John's simple remedy in times of crisis: 'One positive thought produces millions of positive vibrations.'

influences.name: Alice Coltrane
influences.context: I re-immersed myself in the music of John and Alice Coltrane.

influences.name: Jasper Johns
influences.context: I always laugh when I think of Jasper Johns who said, 'One night I dreamed that I painted a large American flag, and the next morning I got up and I went out and bought the materials to begin it.'

influences.name: Sophia Healy
influences.context: There I met one of my art mentors, Sophia Healy, who taught art at the college. She became a seminal influence on both my art and writing.

influences.name: Ken Noland
influences.context: Sophia had worked with Ken Noland when he was experimenting with handmade paper.

influences.name: Joan Mitchell
influences.context: Joan Mitchell's paintings and prints always suck me in with their incredible emotional revelations layered on to nature.

influences.name: Henri Matisse
influences.context: As you may discern from my art, I am influenced by the late work of Matisse, specifically the cut-outs and stencils.

influences.name: Louise Bogan
influences.context: I've finally opted out of the 'knife of the perfectionist attitude in art' (Louise Bogan, 1934)

influences.name: Julia Cameron
influences.context: Many years ago I stumbled upon a free, used copy of 'The Artist's Way' (Julia Cameron)

influences.name: André Gide
influences.context: When I feel hesitant about trying something new, I recall the wise words of André Gide, 'One does not discover new lands without consenting to lose sight of the shore for a very long time.'

influences.name: Bach
influences.context: One of the most difficult tests for a composer is to write a fugue in the style of Bach. What I have loved in my experience of studying historical performance style is that I finally began to understand where the sound comes from, how it developed, what kind of audience was there to listen to early or classical or romantic music, and what the composers wanted to offer their listeners.

influences.name: Mac Miller
influences.context: I have some artists that I listened to a lot, such as Mac Miller. He was a great musician and lyricist.

influences.name: Frank Ocean
influences.context: And I listened to Frank Ocean a lot.

influences.name: Leon the House
influences.context: And I listened to Leon the House a lot.

influences.name: Amy Winehouse
influences.context: I listened to a lot of Amy Winehouse when I was younger.
